I'm sorry. I answered your question in the middle of other work, where it was easy to miss, and then went on without checking you had seen it. Here is the answer first, then what I've been busy with.

## Your question: won't adding tools inflate the context?

Yes, you're right to worry about that. Every tool's definition is sent with the first message of each chat, and the AI already has 32 tools.

Of the six things I proposed, only one is a new tool: text on a model. The other five add a field to a tool that already exists:

- **Adding a filament** is a longer list passed to the existing printer setup tool.
- **Filament change or pause at a height** and **prime tower position** are fields on the existing plate layout tool.
- **Holes** is one more option in the existing region-marking tool.
- **A filament per part** is a field on the plate layout tool.

A field still costs a sentence or two in that tool's description, so it is not free, but it is far less than a whole tool. I would hold the text tool until you decide a 33rd is worth it.

## What I'm busy with

I'm carrying out a change you asked for in a side chat this morning, the one titled [btw: Are we currently blocking user AI from changing some of the...](#local_87d1b808-981e-4818-a005-3d495ad4fcec). There you wrote: "let's keep the first 2 groups blocked. unblocked the other 2. tel lthe main session to do so". That side chat passed it to me, and I found those words in its transcript before starting.

The change is to the list of settings the AI is not allowed to change:

- **Stays blocked:** the setting that runs a program on the computer, and the printer's network address and sign-in.
- **Becomes changeable:** the printer's hardware settings, such as bed size and nozzle size, and the settings that say which presets fit which printer.

So far I've made that edit on a separate branch (`claude/unblock-hardware-settings`), in its own folder, so your main checkout is untouched. Nothing is committed.

The slow part is testing. The project has a test that changes every setting in the real app, one at a time, and checks that nothing breaks. Those 37 settings have never been through it. Running it needs a full build of the app, which is going in the background now and will take two to three hours at four jobs.

## Decision needed

Should I keep going with the settings change? It is yours to call because the build uses four of the Mac's twelve cores for a few hours.

- **Keep going:** I run the test when the build finishes and report any setting that turns out unsafe to change.
- **Stop:** I stop the build now and leave the branch as it is. Nothing is lost except the build time so far.

My pick is to keep going, since you asked for the change and the edit is done. Do you want me to continue?

content.text:
Your feeling is right, and I've changed the proposal: holes, simple shapes and text should be one tool.

## Why they belong together

OrcaSlicer itself treats them as one thing. When a person right-clicks an object, the menu offers Add Part, Add Negative Part and Add Modifier. Each of those opens the same list: Cube, Cylinder, Sphere, Cone, Disc, Torus, Text and SVG. So a person makes two choices, and text is just one of the shapes:

- **What the shape is for:** solid material, or a hole.
- **What the shape is:** a box, a cylinder, or some text.

A screw hole is "hole, cylinder". Raised lettering is "solid, text". Engraved lettering is "hole, text".

## Why I had split them

My reasons were weak:

- The tool guide has an old line saying text gets its own tool. It was written before anyone looked at holes.
- For holes I reached for the region-marking tool, because it already makes boxes and cylinders. But that tool records what a part of the model means, such as "keep the seam off this face". A hole changes the model's shape, which is a different job.

The real difference between them is only in the inputs. Text needs the words, a size, a depth and a spot on a surface, where a box needs a centre and a size.

## What the proposal is now

One tool that adds a shape to an object, taking what it is for and what it is. It is still the only new tool in my list, the same count as before. It would cover all seven people who asked for a shape, a hole, text or a logo. I've updated [ai-feature-coverage.md](ai-feature-coverage.md) to say this.

One thing I have not checked: OrcaSlicer builds text as a background job, and I don't yet know how much of that job works without the text tool's own window open. That decides how hard the text half is.

## The settings change

The build is still running with no errors, about 20 minutes in. I'll run the every-setting test when it finishes and report back.

## Your question: is region marking also just adding geometry?

You're right for half of what that tool does, and that half is enough to change my proposal again.

When the AI marks a region with a box or a cylinder, the tool adds a shape to the object and gives it a type. Today it can give three types: a modifier with its own settings, a support blocker, or a support enforcer. OrcaSlicer keeps those in one list with two more, a solid part and a negative part (a hole). So a hole really is the same operation with a different type, as you said.

The other half is different, but it doesn't change the conclusion. When the AI marks a face, or "every face pointing this way", the tool paints the existing surface and adds no shape. The AI never has to know which of the two happened.

So my proposal is now to add holes, solid shapes and text to the region tool, with **no new tool**. Two things would need settling in the design:

- The tool already has a kind called `precision_hole`. It keeps support out of an existing hole, and would be confused with making one.
- Text is built by OrcaSlicer as a background job. I still have not checked how much of that works without the text tool's own window.

[ai-feature-coverage.md](ai-feature-coverage.md) now says this.

## The settings change

The 37 hardware and compatibility settings are unblocked on branch `claude/unblock-hardware-settings`, and tested in the real app. Nothing is committed.

- **Bed size works end to end.** The test asked for 250, the plate became 250 by 250, and undoing it restored 256.
- **33 of the 37 settings pass the every-setting test.** Each was changed and changed back with no dialog, no other preset switched, and the preset left as it was.
- **Three were not exercised.** `compatible_prints`, `parallel_printheads_bed_exclude_areas` and `extruder_printable_area` either refused my test value or have none I could generate.
- **One fails: `printer_technology`.** The test set it to SLA. The app then reported "No FFF printer is selected", and the tools could not set it back. So one wrong write locks the AI out of the project until the person fixes the printer by hand.

Other results: the two unit test programs pass (615 and 44 test cases), and the page's 839 tests pass. The harness also still fails two checks about dropping a model onto a project. Both were failing before this change.

**Also changed, because they described the old list:**

- The printer chat's instructions now say the nozzle size is changed with `printer_change`, not with a settings change. That wording is my proposal.
- The prompt test "make the bed 250 by 250" now passes when the AI changes the bed. Before, it passed when the AI said it couldn't.
- The tool guide and the saved note on the blocked list.

**Not tested:**

- Saving a preset with a wrong "inherits from" or "fits these printers" value and then restarting the app. That is where a preset could really break.
- The flipped prompt test against a real model. It costs API money, so I have not run it.

## Decision needed

`printer_technology` is one of the 37 you asked me to unblock. JusPrin has no resin printing, so the only thing a write to it can do is break the project, as the test shows. Keeping it blocked makes the list 15 settings instead of 14 and lets the test pass. Leaving it unblocked follows your words exactly, but the every-setting test keeps failing and the branch cannot land as it is. My pick is to keep that one blocked.

You're right that I went along with you. I changed my answer three times in a day, each time on an argument and never on evidence. Here are the facts I checked, then my own position, which is not the one I gave you last.

## Does upstream OrcaSlicer treat them alike in its screens?

Partly. It has two groups.

**One family: things you add to an object.** I read this in the upstream code.

- The right-click menu on an object has these items one after another: Add Part, Add Negative Part, Add Modifier, Add Support Blocker, Add Support Enforcer.
- Each opens the same list of shapes: Cube, Cylinder, Sphere, Cone, Disc, Torus, Text, SVG.
- A Change Type menu turns any one of them into any other. A person can make a solid part into a hole, or into a support blocker, with one click.

So on this half you are right: OrcaSlicer treats a hole, a solid shape, a modifier and a support blocker as one kind of thing with a different type.

**A separate group: painting on the surface.** Support painting, seam painting, colour painting and fuzzy-skin painting are each their own button on the toolbar, with brushes. None of them is in the Add menu. Text also has its own toolbar button, as well as being in the Add list.

## Where I actually stand

I agree with you that holes, solid shapes and text are one capability. OrcaSlicer's menu shows that, and I should have seen it before you asked.

I disagree with putting them in the region tool, which is what I told you an hour ago. My reasons:

- **The region tool never changes the object's shape.** The AI tells it what a region means, such as "keep the seam off this face", and the app decides how to print it. A hole or raised text changes the shape itself, as a cut does.
- **Your own product definition splits them this way.** It lists "text" and "positive/negative parts" with cut, split and merge. It lists "modifiers, support enforcers, blockers" separately.
- **People asked for them the way they ask for cutting.** In the kept chats the words were "add holes for the screws", "add a cube", "put the logo there", next to "remove the name on the bottom". The AI did that last one with the cut tool.

So my pick is one tool for adding a shape to an object, sitting beside the cut and merge tools. I hold that with moderate confidence.

On your context worry, the choice makes little difference. The words that describe holes and text have to be sent to the model wherever they live. A separate tool adds only a name and a small wrapper on top. That is my reading and I have not measured it.

What I can't tell you by arguing is which grouping the model uses correctly. The tool guide says to settle that from real calls, not a design discussion. The test would be to write both versions and run the seven real requests, plus ordinary seam and support requests, and count the wrong picks. It costs API money, so I have not run it.

[ai-feature-coverage.md](ai-feature-coverage.md) now lists both placements, my lean, and that it is not settled.

## The settings change

`printer_technology` stays unblocked, as you said. The every-setting test now records it as the one setting that locks the tools out, and fails if any other setting does the same. The last run of the real-app harness shows only its two old failures, both about dropping a model onto a project.

All seven changed files are on branch `claude/unblock-hardware-settings`, uncommitted. Still not done: the flipped "make the bed 250 by 250" prompt test has not been run against a real model, because it costs API money.

Below is a list of things a person can do to an object in OrcaSlicer's Prepare view. The order is random and means nothing.

4. Add a support blocker shape to an object
5. Move, rotate or scale an object

7. Paint the seam position on the object's surface
8. Add a modifier to an object (a shape whose space gets its own print settings)
9. Merge or assemble several objects into one
10. Add a solid part to an object (a cube, cylinder, sphere and so on)
11. Paint colours (filaments) on the object's surface
12. Split an object into its separate pieces
13. Add a support enforcer shape to an object

15. Add a height range modifier (settings for a band of heights)
16. Add an SVG shape to an object
17. Paint fuzzy skin on the object's surface
18. Change the type of something already added to an object (for example from a solid part to a negative part)

been run against a model.

Not tested: saving a preset with a wrong inherits or compatible_* value and
restarting the app.
EOF
